chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to Ibn Ḥazm that he should send to him the charity endowment of ʿAlī, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān. Ibn Ḥazm then sent to Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan, and he was the eldest of them, and asked him about the charity. So Zayd said: The guardian after ʿAlī was al-Ḥasan, and after al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and after al-Ḥusayn, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and after ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī; so send to him.
So Ibn Ḥazm sent to my father, and my father sent me with the letter to him, until I delivered it to Ibn Ḥazm.

Then some of us said to him: Do the sons of al-Ḥasan recognize this? He said: Yes, just as they recognize that this is night, but envy drives them. If they had sought the truth by the truth, it would have been better for them, but they seek the world.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life or worldly gain sought in place of the truth
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةَ: the charity endowment or charitable property being requested and administered
key_terms.الْحَسَدُ: envy, described as the motive preventing acceptance of the truth
key_terms.الْحَسَنَ: Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, named as the first successor after Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in this report
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the truth that ought to be sought and acknowledged
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ: Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, named as the next successor in the line of authority
key_terms.الْوَالِيَ: the rightful guardian or holder of authority in succession
key_terms.مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ: Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir عليه السلام, identified here as the authority to whom one should refer

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the succession of authority among the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام after Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration recounts a historical episode concerning the administration of charity endowments and identifies the rightful succession of authority after Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام through Imam al-Ḥasan, Imam al-Ḥusayn, Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and Imam Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليهما السلام. It also states that some people recognized this truth but were diverted by envy and worldly motives.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Umar Bin Abdul Aziz (the governor) wrote to Ibn Hazim (the judge) that he should send to him the charity donations record of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and Umar and Usman. And Ibn Hazim (the judge) sent for Zayd son of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and he was their eldest, and he asked him of the charity. So Zayd said, ‘The Guardian after Ali<sup>asws</sup> was Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and after Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, it was Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and after Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> it was Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and after Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> it was Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>azwj</sup>.

Therefore, send (a messenger) to him<sup>asws</sup>. 
So Ibn Hazim (the judge) sent (a messenger) to my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>. So my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> sent me<sup>asws</sup> with the Book to him until I<sup>asws</sup> handed it over to him’.

So one of us said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Did the sons of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> know this?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, just as they were knowing that this is a night, but, the envy carried them, and had they sought the Truth with the Truth, it would have been better for them, but they are seeking the world’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan has narrated from Sahl from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Fadala ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘ala’ who has said that he heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say the following.

“’Umar ibn ‘ad al-‘Aziz wrote ibn Hazm to send him the endowment documents of Ali, ‘Umar and ‘Uthman. Inb Hazm sent a person to Zayd ibn al-Hassan (a.s.) who was the eldest among them and asked him about the documents. Zayd said, “The high authority after Ali was al-Hassan and after him al-Husayn and Ali ibn al-Husayn was after al-Husayn and after Ali ibn al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ali was the high authority. Send to him.
Ibn Hazm then sent to my father and my father sent me with document to him and I went and delivered it to ibn Hazm.”

The narrator has said that some of our people asked The Imam (a.s.), “did the sons of al-Hassan (a.s.) know this.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “They knew it just as they know that this is night but envy influences them. Had they sought truth with truth it would have been better for them but they seek the worldly things. * Abu Baker ibn Muhammad ibn ’Amr ibn Hazm al-Ansari (37/657 -120/738), the judge of Madina from 87/706 appointed by ‘Umar ibn ‘Abdi al-‘Aziz when he was governor of Madina. When ‘Umar became the Caliph he also appointed ibn Hazm governor of Madina. (al-Tabari, vol.2, pp.ll91, 1255, 1305, 1346, 1372 - 1375, 1437, 1452; vol.3, p.2460; ibn al-Athir, vol.5, pp.55,67; Tahdhib al-Takdhib, vol.l2, pp.38 -40.
